normalized.description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. normalized.description: Water Resources Management (WRM) and Disaster Risk Management (DRM) are two thematic areas that are important in Slovenia. In 2025 a preparatory activity concerning the contribution of satellite data for different thematic areas has highlighted the needs of priorities of a group of nationally mandated stakeholders from both the WRM sector and the DRM sector. While the ESA Digital Twin Earth (ESA DTE) programme is looking at integrating Earth Observation (EO) satellite capabilities in future operational Digital Twins ecosystems, including the potential future evolution of DestinE and other operational DT initiatives in Europe, this activity is a precursor development under the FutureEO programme to prepare the ground for an EO based digital ecosystem and connect EO data, processingchains and modelling. This FutureEO activity aims to implement and demonstrate a preliminary Digital Twin Precursor to prefigure potential EO based Digital Twin developments. This ITT refers to implementing an EO-based Digital Twin precursor for the themes Water Resources Management and Disaster Risk Management for Slovenia identified through community consultation and considered to be mature enough to start a large activity. For both WRM and DRM themes, the project shall deliver end-to-end pre-operational solutions, fullyimplemented, conceptually and technically mature, scientifically validated, and fully tested by a representative set of early adopters.

normalized.title: HYDRON HAPS: HAPS-BASED OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.242) EXPRO+
normalized.description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. normalized.title: S3-CL-06 SECURE AUTONOMOUS DISPOSAL INTERFACE SAFETY MODULE - REISSUED
normalized.description: The increase in small satellite missions has intensified the need for compliance to international space debris de-orbiting requirements. To meet these requirements CubeSat-class missions frequently rely on their primary On-Board Computer (OBC) and Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) to activate disposal mechanisms, however deployment and late-mission failures; such as battery degradation, bus freeze, or cyber compromise; can prevent successful disposal execution.This activity addresses this gap through the development of the Secure Autonomous Disposal Interface and Safety Module: a standardised, independent Disposal Trigger Module (DTM) compatible withCubeSat buses from 1U to 16U across a variety of disposal mechanisms. The DTM shall implement two autonomy levels of increasing complexity and prove resilient to spacecraft failures and cyberattacks. The project targets bring the technology to TRL6.

originalText: {"job":"institution-ESA-issued-competition","collectionState":"reconciled","verifiedOpen":false,"spaceRelevance":"not_assessed","recordType":"discovery_candidate","evidence":{"file":"institution-ESA-issued-competition/page-1-3e93065c481114defc2bbc0518b46644be3f23f214b7b0494edc5cfd7943cd54.json","sha256":"3e93065c481114defc2bbc0518b46644be3f23f214b7b0494edc5cfd7943cd54","row":41,"retrievedAt":"2026-11-18T09:23:19.101Z"},"original":{"activityNumber":"1000045329","closingDate":"2027-01-08T13:00:00","clarificationRequestDeadline":"2026-12-25T13:00:00","description":"Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop advanced and post-quantum Subscriber Identity Module (SIMs) for 5G/6G NTN. The focus is to improve user anonymity for robust non-terrestrialnetworks (NTNs) used for governmental applications which have a more urgent need for post-quantum anonymity protection than the commercial market. These SIMs shall implementsecurity improvements of the part of the primary authentication protocol which is implemented in the SIM. Additionally, the corresponding SIM provisioning infrastructure and the corenetwork responsible for the communication with the SIMs will be developed.TargetedImprovements: Enablinga European or Canadian source for robust NTN SIM (Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) or Embedded UICC (eUICC)) for 5G/6G satellite constellation withhardened primary authentication protocolDescription: Current 5G Universal Subscriber Identity Modules (USIMs) to be used in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) for Satellite Communication (SATCOM) terminals lack adequate protectionagainst user tracking when assuming a quantum attacker. While 3GPP is working on the migration to post-quantum cryptography, the privacy needs in governmental NTN networks arehigher than in usual mobile networks and regulatory needs will require the full post-Quantum migration as early as 2030 for governmental communication solutions. An appropriatesolution therefore needs to be developed earlier than the 3GPP timeline foresees.The activity will design, develop and test prototypes of advanced 5G/6G USIMs integrating security improvements to the primary authentication protocol (user tracking enhancements inNTNs and anticipated regulatory requirements for post-quantum cryptography), with all components adhering to GSMA/ETSI security standards and targeting Common Criteria evaluationto prepare for future accreditation.The activity will evaluate two implementation paths to address this need: Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) development, potentially as an applet on an existing smartcard platform, or Embedded UICC (eUICC) with appropriate SIM profiles for multi-provider service access. Post-Quantum Key Exchange Management (KEM) implementations on smartcards prove the technical feasibility of implementing such protocols in the UICC approach.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach.The first phase will study the implementation of post quantum security in the authentication protocol and perform a trade-off analysis between the two implementation paths. It will designand develop an initial prototype of the USIM and provisioning infrastructure compatible with standardised 3GPP interfaces between USIM and Mobile Equipment and perform the designof the security functions of the Core network solution to interoperate with the USIM. The S2NG space segment is expected to comprise of a constellation of two identical satellites (A- and B-units) flying at an altitude of approximately 650 km, in a sun-synchronous orbit. Each satellite will embark a payload comprised of the Advanced Multi-Spectral Imager (AMSI) instrument with two detection chains, one for Visible and Near-Infrared (VNIR) detection and one for the Short Wavelength Infrared (SWIR) detection, with a total of 21 bands (16 in VNIR, 5 in SWIR).The ITT for the Sentinel-2 NG Phases B2/C/D/E1 is in open competition. normalized.description: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation".
